messages.content: Predict one human decision from an experiment with group and individual tasks. The fixed participation fee is 4 GBP and each earned point pays GBP 0.04. The participant is in an anonymous group of three, including self. The group tasks comprise three independent tasks in an individually randomized order. In each task there are four projects, PG1–PG4, shown on one response screen. For EACH project, EACH group member has a separate budget of 10 points and may contribute any whole number from 0 to 10. These are four separate budgets, not one shared 10-point budget; unspent points are kept, and budgets cannot be transferred between projects. For project j, add all three members’ contributions, multiply by its group multiplier Mj, divide equally among the three, then add the participant’s unspent points for that project. A task’s earnings are the sum over all four projects. At the end one of the three tasks is selected uniformly for payment; ALL FOUR projects in that task are paid, and the same task and same project multipliers apply to all three group members. Feedback and realized earnings are given only after the later individual tasks, so no peer choice, multiplier draw, selected paying task or realized payoff is available now. For this current task, each project’s group multiplier is drawn uniformly from its stated range: every value within that range is equally likely. The actual draw is unknown when deciding. Predict the four contributions submitted together. Output only a JSON object with keys PG1, PG2, PG3, PG4 and integer amounts from 0 to 10 each. No explanation.
